Delhi HC: Rekha Gupta v. AAP (AI deepfakes)
Delhi HC Division Bench: ANI v. OpenAI appeal (listed early December)
Delhi HC: Kent RO v. Amazon (keyword ads), interim application
Supreme Court: DPDP Act and RTI amendment challenge

Most DPDP Act duties take effect

cases.name: Challenge to the DPDP Act and the RTI amendment
cases.parties: Venkatesh Nayak v. Union of India (W.P.(C) 177/2026) and connected petitions, including the Digital News Publishers Association
cases.issue: Whether s. 44(3), which narrowed the RTI exemption for personal information, and other provisions (ss. 17, 33, 36 and the Board's selection rules) are constitutional, and whether journalism needs an exemption.
cases.stands: Notice issued and no interim stay. The RTI petitions were referred to a larger bench in February 2026. On 27 October the Court issued notice on the news publishers' petition and declined an interim stay without hearing the Union. The matter was listed with the connected petitions on 17 November but could not be taken up, and was adjourned to 9 December.

cases.name: Digital arrest scams and bank liability
cases.parties: In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents (suo motu)
cases.issue: What banks, the RBI and platforms such as WhatsApp must do to prevent digital arrest frauds, and who compensates victims.
cases.stands: On 29 October the Court said the RBI's new rules must make banks compensate victims where a failure of due diligence enabled the fraud, and that it would examine the draft rules before they are notified. It also asked WhatsApp to propose measures. The order uploaded on 7 November lists the case next on 23 November; some earlier reports gave 30 November.

cases.name: AI deepfakes and political satire
cases.parties: Smt. Rekha Gupta v. Aam Aadmi Party & Ors. (CS(OS) 1019/2026)
cases.issue: Whether AI-generated videos and images of the Delhi Chief Minister posted by a political party are protected satire or defamation.
cases.stands: Interim order of 6 November: six URLs directed to be taken down. Summons issued; the defendants are yet to be heard.

cases.name: AI training and copyright: ANI's appeal
cases.parties: ANI Media Pvt. Ltd. v. OpenAI (appeal against the order of 24 July 2026 in CS(COMM) 1028/2024)
cases.issue: Whether training ChatGPT on ANI's news content is fair dealing for research under s. 52 of the Copyright Act.
cases.stands: The single judge refused ANI an interim injunction on 24 July 2026. A Division Bench issued notice on ANI's appeal on 15 September and gave no interim direction. It is listed in early December; reports give 5 or 8 December.

cases.name: Brand names sold as advertising keywords on Amazon
cases.parties: Kent RO Systems Ltd. v. Amazon Seller Services Pvt. Ltd. (CS(COMM) 1145/2026)
cases.issue: Whether Amazon infringes the well-known mark KENT by letting sellers bid on it as a keyword in its sponsored-products ads, and whether Amazon can claim intermediary safe harbour.
cases.stands: On 16 October Justice Tejas Karia issued summons on Kent's application for an ad interim injunction; Amazon accepted notice. No interim relief has been granted. Amazon's reply is due within three weeks and its written statement within 30 days.

cases.name: Children's safety online
cases.parties: Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish
cases.issue: How to protect children from online sexual exploitation without banning them from the internet.
cases.stands: Order of 15 October 2026: internet access is a fundamental right for children too; blanket age-based bans are disproportionate. The Court directed a child mode, a national hash database, faster takedowns and fines scaled to platform size. The Centre must report progress at the next hearing.

cases.name: Collector's order allegedly drafted with AI
cases.parties: Medipalli Komuraiah v. State of Telangana (writ petition)
cases.issue: Whether a revenue order in a land dispute, allegedly passed ex parte with AI tools and without verifying facts, can stand.
cases.stands: On 3 November Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar suspended the Jangaon Collector's order of 8 September, issued notice to the Revenue Principal Secretary, the Collector and the Tahsildar, and asked the Advocate-General what action is proposed. Listed on 18 November; the outcome has not been reported yet.

cases.name: Facial recognition at protest sites
cases.parties: SFLC.in v. Union of India; A.A. Rahim v. Union of India
cases.issue: Whether police may use facial recognition on people at designated protest sites without a law authorising it.
cases.stands: Notice issued on 3 November 2026 on SFLC.in's petition, tagged with A.A. Rahim's earlier plea on the July Jantar Mantar protests. The Union is yet to reply.

cases.name: Ban on online money games
cases.parties: Head Digital Works v. Union of India and connected cases
cases.issue: Whether Parliament can ban all online money games, including games of skill, under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025.
cases.stands: On 5 August 2026 a bench led by the Chief Justice agreed to a final hearing. There is no interim stay, so the Act (in force since 1 May 2026) applies.
cases.next_note: Final hearing date not yet announced

cases.name: Meta's California clause v. Indian courts
cases.issue: Whether an Indian advertiser's suit over disabled ad accounts must go to California under Meta's terms.
cases.stands: On 27 October the court refused Meta's application: claims under the IT Act and IT Rules need an Indian forum. The suit for restoration and damages continues; jurisdiction can still be argued at trial.

cases.name: Data Protection Board appointments
cases.parties: Not a case: the regulator under the DPDP Act
cases.issue: When the Data Protection Board's Chairperson and Members will be appointed.
cases.stands: The Board was established in law on 13 November 2025, but no Chairperson or Member had been appointed as of mid-November 2026, even as consent manager registration opened on 13 November. The Kerala High Court recorded on 7 October that the Board was not functional.

cases.name: No writ against Meta for blocking an account
cases.parties: Sarthak Bhagat v. Union of India
cases.issue: Can a user challenge Instagram's account block by writ?
cases.stands: 27 October 2026: writ not maintainable against Meta; restoration must be sought by civil suit. The Grievance Appellate Committee was directed to decide the appeal quickly.

cases.name: User must get a copy of a takedown notice
cases.parties: Haryana 24 News Network v. Union of India
cases.issue: Was an SP's s. 79(3)(b) notice that got a news page blocked valid?
cases.stands: Reported 20 October 2026: the notice was without jurisdiction (Rule 3(1)(d) needs a DIG-rank officer), a copy must go to the user, and the page was ordered restored.

cases.name: Platforms can act on copyright complaints
cases.parties: Anmol Jain v. Union of India
cases.issue: Can Instagram suspend a creator's account over copyright complaints without a court order?
cases.stands: 17 September 2026: challenge to Rule 3(1)(b)(iv) dismissed; the grievance officer and GAC are adequate safeguards.

cases.name: Customs penalty built on fake AI citations set aside
cases.parties: Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya v. Union of India
cases.issue: Can an adjudication relying on non-existent cases stand?
cases.stands: 2 September 2026: ₹425 crore penalty set aside and sent back to a different officer; "assistance can never be substituted for adjudication."

cases.name: Fake citations make a decision "no decision at all"
cases.parties: Pooja Ramesh Singh v. J&K Bank Ltd., 2026 INSC 668
cases.issue: Effect of NCLT and NCLAT orders relying on non-existent judgments.
cases.stands: 2 July 2026: both orders set aside; citing AI-generated precedents without verification is professional misconduct; the BCI to frame guidelines.
